title: Just as I Am Without One Plea
description: Just as I Am Without One Plea in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 6 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Charlotte Elliott, first published in 1835. The tune, WOODWORTH, is by William Batchelder Bradbury (1849). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Just_ as I am,_ wi-thout_ one plea, But that_ Thy blood was shed for me, And_ that Thou bid-dest me come to Thee,_ O Lamb of God,_ I come, I come.

lines: Just as I am, without one plea,
But that Thy blood was shed for me,
And that Thou biddest me come to Thee,
Just as I am, and waiting not
To rid my soul of one dark blot,
To Thee, Whose blood can cleanse each spot,
Just as I am, though tossed about
Just as I am, poor, wretched, blind;
Sight riches healing of the mind,
Yea, all I need, in Thee to find,
Just as I am, Thy love unknown
Now to be Thine, yea Thine alone,
O Lamb of God, I come, I come.
